records.literal_gloss: If you love me, the commandments the mine you will keep.

en.B: If you love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you will keep the commandments I have given you.
en.R: If you love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you will obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands.

es.B: Si me {{plural_you:aman|amáis}}, {{plural_you:guardarán|guardaréis}} los mandamientos que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dado.

vi.B: Nếu các con yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, các con sẽ giữ những điều răn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ban cho các con.

ko.L: 너희가 나를 사랑하면, 나의 계명들을 지킬 것이다.
ko.B: 너희가 나를 사랑하면 내가 준 계명을 지킬 것이다.
ko.R: 너희가 나를 사랑하면 내 계명을 지킬 것이다.

decisions.choice: you will keep (future), as the SBLGNT reads
alternatives: that you may keep my commandments
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads τηρήσετε, a future: "you will keep". Many manuscripts, mostly later ones, have instead the command "keep my commandments", and a few early ones read a form meaning "that you may keep". The forms differ by a letter or two and were easily confused in copying. The future fits the way Jesus goes on in 14:21 and 14:23-24, where keeping his word is what love does. A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: love for Jesus shows itself in keeping his commandments
alternatives: obedience as the condition for being loved
decisions.reason: The sentence does not set a price for Jesus's love; it says what love for him looks like. The same link runs through the passage in both directions: whoever keeps his commandments is the one who loves him (14:21), and whoever does not love him does not keep his words (14:24). Compare 1 John 5:3.

decisions.choice: my commandments: all that Jesus has told them, above all the new commandment to love one another
alternatives: the commandments of the Law of Moses
decisions.reason: The Greek stresses that they are his own ("the commandments, the mine"). He has just given the new commandment to love one another as he has loved them (13:34); in 14:23-24 the same thing is called his "word" and his "words". "Keep" means hold on to and obey, as in 8:51.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}, {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}, {{deity_pronoun:we|We}}, {{deity_pronoun:our|Our}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Jesus, for the Father and for the Spirit uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "me", "my" and "myself" when Jesus speaks of himself, "you" when Judas speaks to him (14:22), and "we" and "our" when Jesus speaks of the Father and himself (14:23). At the start of a sentence "He" or "My" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: keep ... commandments (L); keep the commandments I have given you (B); obey my commands (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "keep" and "commandments", the words that tie this verse to 13:34 and 14:21. Balanced spells out that these are commandments Jesus himself has given, which is what the stressed "mine" says. Readable uses the plainer "obey" and "commands".

decisions.choice: guardarán ... mandamientos (L, B); obedecerán mis mandatos (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: amri zangu mtazishika (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order, with "my commandments" before the verb, which the object prefix "-zi-" makes natural in Swahili. "Kushika" (keep) for this verb, as in verses 21, 23 and 24; Readable says "kutii" (obey), as the English says "obey".

decisions.choice: Ta ... các con (Jesus to the disciples)
decisions.reason: As set for the whole book: Jesus says "Ta" of himself (the deity_pronoun span in mid-sentence) and "các con" to his disciples. Recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체), and gives the Father and the Spirit the honorific ("께서", -시-, "그분")
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Recorded once for 14:15-24.

source.text: κἀγὼ ἐρωτήσω τὸν πατέρα καὶ ἄλλον παράκλητον δώσει ὑμῖν ἵνα ᾖ μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, ὃ ὁ κόσμος οὐ δύναται λαβεῖν, ὅτι οὐ θεωρεῖ αὐτὸ οὐδὲ γινώσκει· ὑμεῖς γινώσκετε αὐτό, ὅτι παρ’ ὑμῖν μένει καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν ἔσται.

en.B: I will ask the Father, and in answer {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you another Advocate, who will be with you forever. \v 17 This is the Spirit of truth. The world is not able to receive {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, since it does not see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and does not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But you know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remains with you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be in you.
en.R: I will ask the Father for you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you another Advocate, one like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. He will be with you forever. \v 17 He is the Spirit of truth. The world, which has turned away from God, cannot receive {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because it does not see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} or know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But you know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remains with you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be in you.

vi.B: Ta sẽ xin Cha, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ ban cho các con một Đấng Biện Hộ khác, Đấng sẽ ở với các con mãi mãi. \v 17 Đó là Thánh Linh của chân lý. Thế gian không thể nhận lấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì thế gian không thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và không biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Nhưng các con biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở lại với các con, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ ở trong các con.
vi.R: Ta sẽ xin Cha cho các con, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ ban cho các con một Đấng Biện Hộ khác, giống như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ngài sẽ ở với các con mãi mãi. \v 17 Ngài là Thánh Linh của chân lý. Thế gian, là những người đã quay lưng với Đức Chúa Trời, không thể nhận lấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì họ không thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng không biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Nhưng các con biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở lại với các con, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ ở trong các con.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 아버지께 청하겠고, 그분께서 너희에게 다른 변호자를 주셔서 영원히 너희와 함께 있게 하실 것이다. \v 17 [그분은] 곧 진리의 영이시다. 세상은 그분을 받을 수 없다. 세상이 그분을 보지도 못하고 알지도 못하기 때문이다. 너희는 그분을 안다. 그분께서 너희 곁에 머물러 계시고, 너희 안에 계실 것이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 내가 아버지께 구하면, 아버지께서 너희에게 다른 변호자를 주셔서 영원히 너희와 함께 계시게 하실 것이다. \v 17 그분은 진리의 영이시다. 세상은 그분을 받아들일 수 없다. 세상은 그분을 보지도 못하고 알지도 못하기 때문이다. 그러나 너희는 그분을 안다. 그분께서 너희와 함께 머물러 계시고, 너희 안에 계실 것이기 때문이다.
ko.R: 내가 너희를 위해 아버지께 구하겠다. 그러면 아버지께서 너희에게 다른 변호자, 곧 나와 같은 분을 주실 것이다. 그분은 너희와 영원히 함께 계실 것이다. \v 17 그분은 진리의 영이시다. 하나님을 등진 세상은 그분을 받아들일 수 없다. 세상은 그분을 보지도 못하고 알지도 못하기 때문이다. 그러나 너희는 그분을 안다. 그분께서 너희와 함께 머물러 계시고, 너희 안에 계실 것이기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: another Advocate: a second one of the same kind as Jesus himself
alternatives: an advocate of a different kind
decisions.reason: The word ἄλλον means another of the same sort. Jesus has been with the disciples as their helper, teacher and defender; now that he is going away, the Father will give them another who will do the same for them. 1 John 2:1 uses this same title for Jesus himself, speaking for believers before the Father. And unlike Jesus, who is about to leave them, this one will be with them "forever" (literally "into the age").

decisions.choice: Advocate: one called to stand beside someone and speak for them
decisions.reason: The noun παράκλητον was used of someone called in to stand by a person, especially to speak for them before a court. In John the setting is witness and judgment: the Spirit will testify about Jesus (15:26) and prove the world wrong about sin, righteousness and judgment (16:8-11). "Advocate" keeps that setting; "Helper", "Counselor" and "Comforter" each bring out a part of the word's meaning. This is the first of its four occurrences in John (14:16, 26; 15:26; 16:7).

decisions.choice: the Spirit of truth: the Holy Spirit, who belongs to the truth and leads Jesus's followers into it
alternatives: a spirit or attitude of truthfulness
decisions.reason: This is God's own Spirit, the Advocate just promised, so it is "the Spirit" and not a human spirit or attitude. He is "of truth" because he comes from the God of truth and makes the truth known: he will guide the disciples into all the truth (16:13) and testify about Jesus, who is the truth (14:6; 15:26).

decisions.choice: the neuter pronouns follow the grammar of the word "Spirit"; they do not make the Spirit a thing
decisions.reason: The word for Spirit, πνεῦμα, is neuter in Greek, so the pronouns that refer back to it are neuter too: ὃ ("which"), αὐτὸ and αὐτό ("it"). This is a rule of agreement, like the gender of nouns in many languages, and says nothing about whether the Spirit is a person. The Advocate does what persons do: he teaches and reminds (14:26), testifies (15:26), convicts, guides, hears and speaks (16:8-13); and in 16:13-14 John uses a masculine pronoun ("that one") for him.

decisions.choice: the world: humanity organized against God
alternatives: all people, without that sense of opposition
decisions.reason: Here "the world" is set against the disciples: it cannot receive the Spirit, because it does not see or know him. This is the world that does not know God and turns against Jesus and his followers (1:10; 15:18-19; 17:14, 25). It cannot receive him, not because the Spirit is hidden, but because of what it is.

decisions.choice: he remains with you and will be in you: the Spirit is present with them now, and will live within them
alternatives: two ways of saying the same thing
decisions.reason: "Remains" is John's key verb μένει, used of the Spirit remaining on Jesus (1:32-33) and of believers remaining in Jesus (15:4-10). "With you" and "in you" are not quite the same: the disciples already know the Spirit, who is at work in Jesus among them, but the Spirit will be given to live within them only after Jesus is glorified (7:39; 20:22). The future "will be" points to that time.

decisions.choice: will be in you (future), as the SBLGNT reads
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads ἔσται, "will be". Some early and important manuscripts read the present "is" ("he remains with you and is in you"). The present would make the Spirit's dwelling in the disciples something already true; the future makes it a promise for after Jesus's departure, in line with 7:39 and 16:7. A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: whom, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} for the Spirit; never "it" or "which"
decisions.reason: English pronouns follow the sense, not the grammatical gender of a noun. The Spirit is a person (meaning decision m4), so every level says "he", "him" and "whom", with the deity_pronoun setting as for the Father and the Son. Literal brackets the second "him", which the Greek leaves unstated.

decisions.choice: Advocate, capitalized; forever
decisions.reason: "Advocate" is the book's word for this title at every level (meaning decision m2), capitalized because it names the Spirit. "Into the age" is the Greek idiom for "forever".

decisions.choice: in answer (B); for you, one like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, which has turned away from God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "in answer" and Readable "for you" to make plain how the two halves of the first clause are linked: the Father gives because the Son asks, and he asks on the disciples' behalf. Readable also explains "another" as "one like me" (meaning decision m1) and says which world is meant (meaning decision m5), since a young reader would take "the world" to mean simply everyone. It keeps the word "world".

decisions.choice: Defensor, capitalised; para siempre
decisions.reason: One called to stand beside someone and speak for them (meaning decision m2). "Consolador" is the traditional Spanish word but names only part of the sense; "Abogado" sounds like a courtroom profession; "Paráclito" is a transliteration few readers know.

decisions.choice: al cual, lo, él for the Spirit
decisions.reason: Spanish "Espíritu" is masculine, so the pronouns are personal without any change (meaning decision m4). The clitic "lo" is not under the setting; the stressed "él" for the Father is.

decisions.choice: Mtetezi, capitalised
decisions.reason: The meaning note: one called to stand beside someone and speak for them. "Mtetezi" (defender, one who pleads another's case) carries that, as the English "Advocate" does; "Msaidizi" (helper) and "Mfariji" (comforter) each keep only one side of it. Capitalised as a title of the Holy Spirit. The same in verse 26.

decisions.choice: personal agreement for Roho (ambaye, kumpokea, anakaa); naye with a deity_pronoun span
alternatives: kiambaye / -ki- agreement with roho as a thing
decisions.reason: As the meaning note says, the neuter pronouns of the Greek follow the grammar of the word "Spirit" and do not make the Spirit a thing. Swahili gives Roho personal agreement, as in 7:39, so the free pronoun "naye" carries the same reader setting as the English "he"; a pronoun at the start of a sentence stays plain.

decisions.choice: Đấng Biện Hộ
decisions.reason: Parakletos is one called to stand beside someone and speak for them; John's setting is testimony and judgment, so the book-wide term is "Đấng Biện Hộ" (the Advocate) at every level. "Đấng" marks a person. The footnote gives the familiar "Đấng Yên Ủi" (Comforter) and "Đấng Trợ Giúp" (Helper).

decisions.choice: Thánh Linh của chân lý; "Đấng mà" and "Ngài" for the Spirit
decisions.reason: "Thánh Linh" is the book-wide word for the Spirit and "chân lý" for truth. The Spirit is a person, so the relative is "Đấng mà" and the pronoun "Ngài" under the deity_pronoun setting, never "nó" or "điều".

decisions.choice: "변호자" at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide Korean term for the paraklētos (style guide, section 6): John's setting is testimony and judgment, and "변호자" is one who stands beside someone and speaks for them. "보혜사" is the word of familiar Korean versions but is opaque to most readers today.

decisions.choice: "그분" with the honorific ("계시다", "께서") for the Spirit
decisions.reason: The Greek pronouns are neuter only because "pneuma" is (meaning decision); Korean speaks of the Spirit as a person, with the honorific used for God, at every level.

records.literal_gloss: Not I will leave you orphans, I am coming to you.

en.L: I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you.
en.B: I will not leave you like orphans with no father; I am coming to you.
en.R: I will not leave you all alone, like children who have no father. I am coming to you.

vi.L: Ta sẽ không để các con mồ côi; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến với các con.
vi.B: Ta sẽ không bỏ các con lại như những đứa trẻ mồ côi không cha; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đến với các con.
vi.R: Ta sẽ không bỏ các con lại một mình, như những đứa trẻ không có cha. Ta sẽ đến với các con.

ko.L: 내가 너희를 고아로 버려두지 않을 것이다. 내가 너희에게 온다.
ko.B: 나는 너희를 아버지 없는 고아처럼 버려두지 않겠다. 내가 너희에게 온다.
ko.R: 나는 너희를 아버지 없는 아이들처럼 외롭게 버려두지 않겠다. 내가 너희에게 온다.

decisions.choice: orphans: children left without a father, bereft and unprotected
decisions.reason: The word ὀρφανούς means children who have lost a parent, and more widely anyone left without a protector. The picture fits: Jesus has called the disciples "little children" (13:33), and a teacher's disciples could be spoken of as his children. Jesus is about to leave them, but they will not be left without a father's care.

decisions.choice: I am coming to you: above all his return to them after the resurrection, continued in his presence through the Spirit
alternatives: his coming in the Spirit only
his coming at the end of the age (14:3)
decisions.reason: The next verse says that in a little while the world will no longer see him but they will see him (14:19), which points to the risen Jesus coming and standing among them (20:19, 26). But the coming is tied to the promise of the Spirit just before (14:16-17), and in 14:23 the Father and the Son come to make their home with the one who loves Jesus, which is not limited to Easter. In 14:3 "I am coming again" speaks of his final coming. The senses may overlap, and the decision between them is not certain.

decisions.choice: I am coming: present tense of a coming that is certain and near
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the present, as in 14:3, for something about to happen and already as good as begun.

decisions.choice: like orphans with no father (B); all alone, like children who have no father (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the picture of children left without a father (meaning decision m1) and say it plainly, so that it is not heard as a legal term only. Literal says "orphans".

decisions.choice: como huérfanos sin padre (B); solos, como niños que no tienen padre (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Ta đến (L), without "sẽ"
decisions.reason: The Greek present tense of a sure and near coming; Literal leaves out the future word "sẽ", which Balanced and Readable add.

source.text: ἔτι μικρὸν καὶ ὁ κόσμος με οὐκέτι θεωρεῖ, ὑμεῖς δὲ θεωρεῖτέ με, ὅτι ἐγὼ ζῶ καὶ ὑμεῖς ζήσετε.

records.literal_gloss: Yet a little and the world me no longer sees, but you see me, because I live and you will live.

en.L: Yet a little [while] and the world no longer sees {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but you see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; because I live, you also will live.
en.B: In a short time the world will no longer see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but you will see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Because I live, you too will live.
en.R: Soon the world will not see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} anymore. But you will see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Because I am alive, you will have life too.

es.L: Todavía un poco, y el mundo ya no me ve, pero {{plural_you:ustedes me ven|vosotros me veis}}; porque yo vivo, también {{plural_you:ustedes vivirán|vosotros viviréis}}.
es.B: Dentro de poco el mundo ya no me verá, pero {{plural_you:ustedes me verán|vosotros me veréis}}. Porque yo vivo, también {{plural_you:ustedes vivirán|vosotros viviréis}}.
es.R: Pronto el mundo ya no me verá. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes me verán|vosotros me veréis}}. Porque yo estoy vivo, también {{plural_you:ustedes tendrán|vosotros tendréis}} vida.

sw.L: Bado muda mfupi, kisha ulimwengu haunioni tena, bali ninyi mnaniona; kwa kuwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninaishi, ninyi pia mtaishi.
sw.B: Baada ya muda mfupi ulimwengu hautaniona tena, lakini ninyi mtaniona. Kwa kuwa ninaishi, ninyi pia mtaishi.
sw.R: Hivi karibuni ulimwengu hautaniona tena. Lakini ninyi mtaniona. Kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni hai, ninyi pia mtakuwa na uzima.

vi.L: Còn ít lâu nữa, thế gian không còn thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nữa, nhưng các con thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sống, các con cũng sẽ sống.
vi.B: Ít lâu nữa thế gian sẽ không còn thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nhưng các con sẽ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sống, các con cũng sẽ sống.
vi.R: Chẳng bao lâu nữa thế gian sẽ không thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nữa. Nhưng các con sẽ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang sống, các con cũng sẽ có sự sống.

ko.L: 조금 [있으면] 세상은 더 이상 나를 보지 못한다. 그러나 너희는 나를 본다. 내가 살기 때문에 너희도 살 것이다.
ko.B: 조금 있으면 세상은 더 이상 나를 보지 못하겠지만, 너희는 나를 볼 것이다. 내가 살아 있으니 너희도 살 것이다.
ko.R: 곧 세상은 나를 더 이상 보지 못할 것이다. 그러나 너희는 나를 볼 것이다. 내가 살아 있으니 너희도 살게 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: a little while, and the world will no longer see me: his death is near, and after it only his disciples will see him
decisions.reason: "Yet a little" means in a short time, as in 13:33 and 16:16-19. The present tenses "sees" speak of what is about to happen. After his death the world will not see Jesus again; the risen Jesus shows himself only to his disciples (20:19-29; 21:1), which is the question Judas raises in 14:22.

decisions.choice: because I live, you also will live: the reason clause goes with what follows it
alternatives: you see me, because I live and you will live
decisions.reason: The word ὅτι can begin a new statement ("because I live, you will live") or give the reason they will see him ("you will see me, because I live and you will live"). The first is the more natural balance of the two short clauses, and it states a theme of the Gospel: the life of believers depends on the life of Jesus (6:57; 11:25-26). Either way, his rising is the ground of their seeing and their living.

decisions.choice: I live ... you will live: Jesus's risen life, which he shares with those who believe
decisions.reason: "I live" is in the present: Jesus has life in himself (5:26), which death cannot hold. "You will live" is the eternal life he gives, which begins now and does not end with death (11:25-26).

decisions.choice: the world: humanity that has rejected Jesus
decisions.reason: As in 14:17, the world here is set against the disciples: those who do not believe in him and will not see him again after his death.

decisions.choice: will see (B, R); I am alive ... you will have life (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the present "sees" into the future, since it speaks of the days after his death (meaning decision m1). Readable says "I am alive" and "you will have life" to make clear that real life, not simply staying alive, is meant.

decisions.choice: me verá ... me verán
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ γνώσεσθε ὑμεῖς ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ πατρί μου καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν ἐμοὶ κἀγὼ ἐν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: In that the day will know you that I in the Father of me and you in me and I in you.

en.L: In that day you will know that I [am] in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and you in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I in you.
en.B: On that day you will come to know that I am in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and that you are in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and I am in you.
en.R: When that day comes, you will understand that I am in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father. You will understand that you are in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and that I am in you.

es.L: En aquel día {{plural_you:conocerán|conoceréis}} que yo [estoy] en mi Padre, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y yo en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: En aquel día {{plural_you:llegarán|llegaréis}} a saber que yo estoy en mi Padre, y que {{plural_you:ustedes están|vosotros estáis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y yo estoy en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Cuando llegue ese día, {{plural_you:entenderán|entenderéis}} que yo estoy en mi Padre. {{plural_you:Entenderán|Entenderéis}} que {{plural_you:ustedes están|vosotros estáis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y que yo estoy en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Katika siku hiyo mtafahamu kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [niko] ndani ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, na ninyi [mko] ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, na {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndani yenu.
sw.B: Siku hiyo mtakuja kujua kwamba niko ndani ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, na kwamba ninyi mko ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} niko ndani yenu.
sw.R: Siku hiyo itakapofika, mtaelewa kwamba niko ndani ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Mtaelewa kwamba ninyi mko ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, na kwamba niko ndani yenu.

vi.L: Trong ngày đó các con sẽ biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [ở] trong Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và các con [ở] trong {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [ở] trong các con.
vi.B: Vào ngày đó, các con sẽ biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trong Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, các con ở trong {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trong các con.
vi.R: Khi ngày đó đến, các con sẽ hiểu rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trong Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Các con sẽ hiểu rằng các con ở trong {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trong các con.

ko.L: 그날에 너희는 내가 내 아버지 안에, 그리고 너희가 내 안에, 그리고 내가 너희 안에 [있다는 것을] 알 것이다.
ko.B: 그날에 너희는 내가 내 아버지 안에 있고, 너희가 내 안에 있으며, 내가 너희 안에 있다는 것을 알게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 그날이 오면 너희는 내가 내 아버지 안에 있다는 것을 깨닫게 될 것이다. 또 너희가 내 안에 있고, 내가 너희 안에 있다는 것도 깨닫게 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: that day: the time after the resurrection, when they see him again and receive the Spirit
alternatives: the last day, at the end of the age
decisions.reason: In the farewell words "that day" is the time that follows the "little while" of 14:19 and 16:16, when their grief turns to joy and they ask the Father in Jesus's name (16:22-26). It begins when the risen Jesus comes to them and breathes the Spirit on them (20:19-22).

decisions.choice: I in my Father, you in me, I in you: the bond of Father and Son is opened to the disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus has just said that he is in the Father and the Father in him (14:10-11). Now the disciples are drawn into that union: they are in him and he is in them, as the vine and the branches (15:4-5) and as he prays in 17:21-23. What they cannot grasp now they will come to know when it is true of them.

decisions.choice: you will know: come to understand from their own experience
decisions.reason: The verb γνώσεσθε is the ordinary "know"; here it is the knowing that comes when what was promised has happened (compare 8:28; 13:7).

decisions.choice: [am] (L); come to know, am, are, and that (B); you will understand ... and that (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb in the clauses after "that". Literal brackets the first "am" and leaves the rest as the Greek has it; Balanced supplies the verbs and says "come to know" for the knowing of experience (meaning decision m3); Readable breaks the sentence in two and repeats "you will understand" so that each clause is clear. The Literal wording is the only natural way to follow the Greek word for word.

decisions.choice: [estoy] (L); llegarán a saber (B); entenderán (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m3).

source.text: ὁ ἔχων τὰς ἐντολάς μου καὶ τηρῶν αὐτὰς ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν ὁ ἀγαπῶν με· ὁ δὲ ἀγαπῶν με ἀγαπηθήσεται ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου, κἀγὼ ἀγαπήσω αὐτὸν καὶ ἐμφανίσω αὐτῷ ἐμαυτόν.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] having the commandments of me and keeping them, that one is the [one] loving me; and the [one] loving me will be loved by the Father of me, and I will love him and will show to him myself.

en.L: The one who has {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and keeps them, that one is the one who loves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; and the one who loves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will be loved by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and I will love {{gender:them|him}} and will show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} to {{gender:them|him}}."
en.B: Whoever has {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and keeps them, that person is the one who loves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Whoever loves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will be loved by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father; I in turn will love {{gender:them|him}} and show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} to {{gender:them|him}}."
en.R: Anyone who knows {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands and obeys them is the person who really loves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. My Father will love everyone who loves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will love {{gender:them|him}} too, and I will show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} to {{gender:them|him}}."

es.L: El que tiene mis mandamientos y los guarda, ese es el que me ama; y el que me ama será amado por mi Padre, y yo lo amaré y me manifestaré a {{gender:esa persona|él}}».
es.B: El que tiene mis mandamientos y los guarda, ese es el que me ama. Al que me ama lo amará mi Padre; y yo también lo amaré y me manifestaré a {{gender:esa persona|él}}».
es.R: El que conoce mis mandatos y los obedece es el que de verdad me ama. Mi Padre amará a todo el que me ama. Yo también lo amaré, y me mostraré a {{gender:esa persona|él}}».

sw.L: Mtu aliye na amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} na kuzishika, yeye ndiye mwenye kunipenda; na mwenye kunipenda atapendwa na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, na {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitampenda na kujionyesha kwake."
sw.B: Yeyote aliye na amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} na kuzishika, huyo ndiye anayenipenda. Yeyote anayenipenda atapendwa na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} kwa upande {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} nitampenda na kujionyesha kwake."
sw.R: Mtu anayezijua amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} na kuzitii ndiye anayenipenda kweli. Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} atampenda kila anayenipenda. Nami pia nitampenda, na nitajionyesha kwake."

vi.L: Người nào có các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và giữ lấy, người ấy là người yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; và người yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} yêu thương, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ yêu thương người ấy và sẽ tỏ mình ra cho người ấy."
vi.B: Ai có các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và giữ lấy, người ấy là người yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ai yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} yêu thương; và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ yêu thương người ấy và tỏ mình ra cho người ấy."
vi.R: Ai biết các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và vâng giữ, người ấy mới thật là người yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ yêu thương mọi người yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta cũng sẽ yêu thương người ấy, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ tỏ mình ra cho người ấy."

ko.L: 나의 계명들을 가지고 그것들을 지키는 사람, 그 사람이 나를 사랑하는 사람이다. 그리고 나를 사랑하는 사람은 내 아버지께 사랑을 받을 것이고, 나도 그를 사랑하여 그에게 나 자신을 드러낼 것이다."
ko.B: 내 계명을 받아 지키는 사람, 바로 그 사람이 나를 사랑하는 사람이다. 나를 사랑하는 사람은 내 아버지께 사랑을 받을 것이고, 나도 그 사람을 사랑하여 그에게 나를 드러낼 것이다."
ko.R: 내 계명을 알고 지키는 사람이 정말로 나를 사랑하는 사람이다. 나를 사랑하는 사람은 누구든지 내 아버지께서 사랑하실 것이다. 나도 그 사람을 사랑하고, 그에게 나를 보여 줄 것이다."

decisions.choice: has my commandments: has received them and holds them as his own
decisions.reason: To "have" his commandments is to have been given them and to hold on to them; "keeps them" adds that they are carried out. Jesus has given his commandments to these disciples (13:34; 15:10-12).

decisions.choice: that one is the one who loves me: love for Jesus is known by keeping his commandments
decisions.reason: The pronoun ἐκεῖνός ("that one") points back with emphasis: it is this person, and no other, who loves him. The sentence turns 14:15 around: there love leads to keeping, here keeping shows the love.

decisions.choice: will be loved by my Father: the Father's love rests on those who love the Son
alternatives: the Father begins to love them only because they love the Son
decisions.reason: This does not mean the love is earned: God loved the world first (3:16). It means that those who love the Son are taken into the love of the Father and the Son for each other (16:27; 17:23, 26).

decisions.choice: show myself: make himself plainly seen and known
decisions.reason: The verb ἐμφανίσω means to make visible or make known. Jesus will show himself to the one who loves him, not to the world (14:19). The risen Jesus did appear to his disciples (20:19-29), and he will also make himself known through the Spirit (14:23, 26). Judas takes up the same verb in 14:22.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The one who loves Jesus may be a man or a woman, so the pronouns for that person use the gender setting.

decisions.choice: show myself (all levels); knows my commands (R)
decisions.reason: "Show" is a plain word for this verb, and every level uses it again in 14:22, so that Judas is heard repeating what Jesus has just said. Readable says "knows" for "has" (meaning decision m1) and adds "really" for the emphasis of "that one" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{gender:esa persona|él}}
decisions.reason: The stressed pronoun after "a" is generic (anyone who loves Jesus), so it takes the gender setting; the clitic "lo" does not.

decisions.choice: me manifestaré (L, B); me mostraré (R)
decisions.reason: Make himself plainly seen and known (meaning decision m4); Judas takes up the verb in verse 22.

decisions.choice: kujionyesha (show myself)
decisions.reason: The meaning note: to make himself plainly seen and known. "Kujionyesha" is the everyday word for this; the same verb answers Judas's question in verse 22.

decisions.choice: người ấy, with no gender span
decisions.reason: Where the English offers "them" or "him", Vietnamese "người ấy" (that person) already includes men and women, so no gender setting is needed; likewise in verse 23.

decisions.choice: no gender spans: "그", "그 사람" (14:21, 23)
alternatives: gender setting spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" and "그" here include men and women alike, and Korean has no separate pronoun to switch to (style guide, section 7), so the gender setting has nothing to change.

source.text: λέγει αὐτῷ Ἰούδας, οὐχ ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης· Κύριε, τί γέγονεν ὅτι ἡμῖν μέλλεις ἐμφανίζειν σεαυτὸν καὶ οὐχὶ τῷ κόσμῳ;

records.literal_gloss: Says to him Judas, not the Iscariot, "Lord, what has happened that to us you are about to show yourself and not to the world?"

en.L: Judas (not the Iscariot) says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, what has happened, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are going to show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} to us and not to the world?"
en.B: Judas (not Judas Iscariot) said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, how is it that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} to us, but not to the world?"
en.R: Another of the disciples named Judas (not Judas Iscariot) asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, why will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} only to us? Why not to the world?"

es.L: Le dice Judas (no el Iscariote): «Señor, ¿qué ha pasado para que te vayas a manifestar a nosotros y no al mundo?».
es.B: Judas (no Judas Iscariote) le dijo: «Señor, ¿cómo es que te vas a manifestar a nosotros y no al mundo?».
es.R: Otro de los discípulos, llamado Judas (no Judas Iscariote), le preguntó: «Señor, ¿por qué te vas a mostrar solo a nosotros? ¿Por qué no al mundo?».

sw.L: Yuda (si yule Iskariote) anamwambia, "Bwana, imekuwaje kwamba utajionyesha kwetu wala si kwa ulimwengu?"
sw.B: Yuda (si Yuda Iskariote) akamwambia, "Bwana, inakuwaje kwamba utajionyesha kwetu, lakini si kwa ulimwengu?"
sw.R: Mwanafunzi mwingine aitwaye Yuda (si Yuda Iskariote) akamwuliza, "Bwana, kwa nini utajionyesha kwetu tu? Kwa nini si kwa ulimwengu?"

vi.L: Giu-đa (không phải Ích-ca-ri-ốt) thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Chúa, đã xảy ra điều gì mà Chúa sắp tỏ mình ra cho chúng con, mà không cho thế gian?"
vi.B: Giu-đa (không phải Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt) thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Chúa, sao Chúa sẽ tỏ mình ra cho chúng con mà không cho thế gian?"
vi.R: Một môn đồ khác cũng tên là Giu-đa (không phải Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt) hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Chúa, tại sao Chúa chỉ tỏ mình ra cho chúng con thôi? Sao không tỏ cho thế gian?"

ko.L: 가룟이 아닌 유다가 그분께 말한다. "주님, 무슨 일이 있기에 우리에게는 자신을 드러내려 하시고 세상에는 그러지 않으십니까?"
ko.B: 가룟 유다가 아닌 다른 유다가 예수께 말했다. "주님, 어떻게 된 일입니까? 왜 우리에게는 자신을 드러내시고 세상에는 드러내지 않으시려는 것입니까?"
ko.R: 제자들 가운데 가룟 유다가 아닌 또 다른 유다가 예수께 여쭈었다. "주님, 왜 우리에게만 나타나시고 세상에는 나타나지 않으려고 하십니까?"

decisions.choice: Judas, not Iscariot: the disciple Luke calls "Judas of James"
decisions.reason: Luke's lists of the Twelve include a second Judas, "Judas of James" (Luke 6:16; Acts 1:13), which may mean son of James. Mark 3:18 and Matthew 10:3 have Thaddaeus in that place, which suggests the same man was known by two names, though this is not certain. John adds "not Iscariot" because Judas Iscariot has already left the room (13:30).

decisions.choice: what has happened that: how can it be, what has changed, that
decisions.reason: The question asks what has come about to make Jesus act this way. Judas seems to expect that the Messiah will show himself openly to all, as Jesus's brothers once urged him to show himself to the world (7:4).

decisions.choice: the world: people in general, those outside the circle of disciples
decisions.reason: In Judas's mouth "the world" means everyone else, the public; he does not yet see what Jesus has said about the world that cannot receive the Spirit (14:17). Jesus answers by saying to whom he and the Father will come (14:23).

decisions.choice: says (L); said, asked (B, R)
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present tense ("says") to make a scene vivid. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told, and Readable says "asked" because Judas asks a question. This is the only such verb in the passage.

decisions.choice: not Judas Iscariot (B, R); Another of the disciples named Judas (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the name so that "Iscariot" is clearly a name for the other Judas. Readable says this is another disciple, which the narrative makes clear (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("dice", "ven"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: Otro de los discípulos, llamado Judas
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "Thưa Chúa", then "Chúa" for "you" and "chúng con" for "us"; no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: A disciple addressing Jesus as kyrie goes on with the noun "Chúa" instead of a pronoun; it is always capitalised, so the English deity_pronoun spans on "you" and "yourself" have no Vietnamese counterpart.

decisions.choice: Judas speaks in 합쇼체 with "주님"; "말한다" (L, historic present), "말했다" (B), "여쭈었다" (R)
decisions.reason: Disciples speak to Jesus in 합쇼체 (style guide, section 4); Literal keeps John's present tense in narrative, as at 14:5-9.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἐάν τις ἀγαπᾷ με τὸν λόγον μου τηρήσει, καὶ ὁ πατήρ μου ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν, καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐλευσόμεθα καὶ μονὴν παρ’ αὐτῷ ποιησόμεθα.

records.literal_gloss: Answered Jesus and said to him, "If anyone loves me, the word of me he will keep, and the Father of me will love him, and to him we will come and a dwelling place with him we will make."

en.L: Jesus answered and said to him, "If anyone loves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{gender:they|he}} will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father will love {{gender:them|him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:we|We}} will come to {{gender:them|him}} and make [a] dwelling place with {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: Jesus replied, "Anyone who loves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word. My Father will love {{gender:them|him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:we|We}} will come to {{gender:them|him}} and make {{deity_pronoun:our|Our}} dwelling place with {{gender:them|him}}.
en.R: Jesus answered, "Anyone who loves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching. My Father will love {{gender:them|him}}. And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father and I will come to {{gender:them|him}} and make {{deity_pronoun:our|Our}} home with {{gender:them|him}}.

es.L: Respondió Jesús y le dijo: «Si alguno me ama, guardará mi palabra, y mi Padre lo amará, y vendremos a {{gender:esa persona|él}} y haremos morada con {{gender:ella|él}}.
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «El que me ama guardará mi palabra. Mi Padre lo amará, y vendremos a {{gender:esa persona|él}} y haremos nuestra morada con {{gender:ella|él}}.
es.R: Jesús le respondió: «El que me ama obedecerá mi enseñanza. Mi Padre lo amará. Y mi Padre y yo vendremos a {{gender:esa persona|él}} y haremos nuestro hogar con {{gender:ella|él}}.

sw.L: Yesu akajibu na kumwambia, "Ikiwa mtu yeyote ananipenda, atalishika neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} atampenda, na {{deity_pronoun:sisi|Sisi}} tutakuja kwake na kufanya makao pamoja naye.
sw.B: Yesu akajibu, "Yeyote anayenipenda atalishika neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} atampenda, {{deity_pronoun:nasi|Nasi}} tutakuja kwake na kufanya makao {{deity_pronoun:yetu|Yetu}} pamoja naye.
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Yeyote anayenipenda atayatii mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} atampenda. Na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} tutakuja kwake na kuishi pamoja naye.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp và nói với ông: "Nếu ai yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, người ấy sẽ giữ lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ yêu thương người ấy, và [Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đến với người ấy và lập chỗ ở với người ấy.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Ai yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ giữ lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ yêu thương người ấy, và Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đến với người ấy và lập chỗ ở nơi người ấy.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Ai yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ vâng giữ lời dạy của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ yêu thương người ấy. Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đến và ở cùng người ấy.

ko.L: 예수께서 대답하여 그에게 말씀하셨다. "누구든지 나를 사랑하면 내 말을 지킬 것이다. 그러면 내 아버지께서 그를 사랑하실 것이고, 우리가 그에게 와서 그의 곁에 머무를 곳을 만들 것이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "나를 사랑하는 사람은 누구든지 내 말을 지킬 것이다. 내 아버지께서 그 사람을 사랑하실 것이고, 우리가 그에게 와서 그와 함께 머무를 곳을 마련할 것이다.
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "나를 사랑하는 사람은 누구든지 내 가르침을 지킬 것이다. 내 아버지께서 그 사람을 사랑하실 것이다. 그리고 아버지와 내가 그 사람에게 가서 그와 함께 살 것이다.

decisions.choice: if anyone loves me, he will keep my word: true of every believer, not only the Eleven
decisions.reason: Jesus answers Judas by widening the promise: "anyone" who loves him. The answer does not say why he will not show himself to the world, but to whom he will show himself: to those whose love for him is seen in keeping his word (14:15, 21).

decisions.choice: my word: the whole of Jesus's message
decisions.reason: The singular "word" is his teaching taken as a whole (8:31, 51; 17:6); in 14:24 the plural "words" means the same teaching in its many sayings, and "commandments" in 14:15, 21 says the same thing from another side.

decisions.choice: we will come and make our dwelling with him: the Father and the Son will live with the believer
alternatives: a coming only at the end of the age
decisions.reason: "We" is the Father and the Son together. This is how Jesus will show himself to those who love him and not to the world (14:22): not by a public display but by coming to live with them, through the Spirit who will be in them (14:17).

decisions.choice: dwelling place: the same word as the "dwelling places" in the Father's house (14:2)
decisions.reason: The noun μονὴν is used in the New Testament only here and in 14:2, and comes from the verb "remain". In 14:2 Jesus goes to prepare a place for the disciples among the many dwelling places in his Father's house; here the Father and the Son make their dwelling with the one who loves him. The promise runs both ways, and the shared word keeps the two verses together. It is a lasting home, not a short stay.

decisions.choice: Jesus replied (B); Jesus answered (R)
alternatives: Jesus answered and said to him (Literal)
decisions.reason: "Answered and said" is a common Greek way of introducing a reply; Balanced and Readable use one verb. It is clear who is being answered.

decisions.choice: [a] dwelling place (L); our dwelling place (B); our home (R); my word (L, B); my teaching (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "dwelling place" so that the reader can see the link with "dwelling places" in 14:2 (meaning decision m4). Readable says "home", the plain word, and names "my Father and I" for "we" (meaning decision m3); it says "teaching" for "word" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{gender:they|he}}, {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: "Anyone" may be a man or a woman, so the pronouns for that person use the gender setting. "Him" in "said to him" is Judas and takes no span.

decisions.choice: morada (L, B); nuestro hogar (R); mi palabra (L, B); mi enseñanza (R)
decisions.reason: "Morada" is the word of 14:2, so the link with the Father's house can be seen (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: {{gender:esa persona|él}} ... {{gender:ella|él}}
decisions.reason: Anyone who loves Jesus (meaning decision m1). The stressed pronouns take the gender setting; "lo" is a clitic and does not. The "we" is in the verb, so there is no pronoun to mark.

decisions.choice: makao (L, B); kuishi pamoja naye (R)
decisions.reason: The same word as the "dwelling places" of verse 2 (meaning note m4), so the same Swahili, "makao": the home the Father prepares and the home he and the Son make with the believer. Readable says "live with them". The free pronouns for the Father and the Son ("sisi", "nasi", "yetu") carry the reader setting, as the English "we" and "our" do.

decisions.choice: [Cha Ta và] Ta (L); Cha Ta với Ta (B); Cha Ta và Ta (R) for "we"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has no fitting "we" here: "chúng ta" would include the listener, and "chúng tôi" is an ordinary human speaker's word. So the "we" of the Father and the Son is spelled out, bracketed at Literal.

decisions.choice: chỗ ở
decisions.reason: The same word as the "chỗ ở" in the Father's house (14:2), as the meaning note points out.

decisions.choice: "머무를 곳" (L, B), as in 14:2; "함께 살 것이다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that this is the same word as the dwelling places of 14:2; Literal and Balanced repeat "머무를 곳" so the reader hears the echo.

source.text: ὁ μὴ ἀγαπῶν με τοὺς λόγους μου οὐ τηρεῖ· καὶ ὁ λόγος ὃν ἀκούετε οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸς ἀλλὰ τοῦ πέμψαντός με πατρός.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] not loving me the words of me not keeps; and the word which you hear not is mine but of the having sent me Father.

en.L: The one who does not love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} does not keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words; and the word that you hear is not {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} but [is] of the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Anyone who does not love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} does not keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words. And the word you are hearing is not {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}; it belongs to the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Anyone who does not love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} does not obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching. And the message you are hearing does not come from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. It comes from the Father, who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: El que no me ama no guarda mis palabras; y la palabra que {{plural_you:oyen|oís}} no es mía, sino del Padre que me envió.
es.B: El que no me ama no guarda mis palabras. Y la palabra que {{plural_you:están oyendo|estáis oyendo}} no es mía; es del Padre que me envió.
es.R: El que no me ama no obedece mi enseñanza. Y el mensaje que {{plural_you:están oyendo|estáis oyendo}} no viene de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Viene del Padre, que me envió.

sw.L: Asiyenipenda hayashiki maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; na neno mnalolisikia si {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, bali ni la Baba aliyenituma.
sw.B: Yeyote asiyenipenda hayashiki maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Na neno mnalolisikia si {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}; ni la Baba aliyenituma.
sw.R: Yeyote asiyenipenda hayatii mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Na ujumbe mnaousikia hautoki {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}. Unatoka kwa Baba, aliyenituma.

vi.L: Người không yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không giữ các lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; và lời mà các con nghe không phải của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nhưng [là] của Cha, Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Ai không yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không giữ các lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Và lời các con đang nghe không phải là của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nhưng thuộc về Cha, Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Ai không yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không vâng giữ lời dạy của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Và lời các con đang nghe không phải đến từ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Lời ấy đến từ Cha, Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 나를 사랑하지 않는 사람은 내 말들을 지키지 않는다. 그리고 너희가 듣는 말은 내 것이 아니라 나를 보내신 아버지의 것이다.
ko.B: 나를 사랑하지 않는 사람은 내 말을 지키지 않는다. 너희가 듣고 있는 이 말은 내 것이 아니라, 나를 보내신 아버지의 말씀이다.
ko.R: 나를 사랑하지 않는 사람은 내 가르침을 지키지 않는다. 너희가 듣고 있는 말은 나에게서 나온 것이 아니다. 나를 보내신 아버지께로부터 나온 것이다.

decisions.choice: whoever does not love me does not keep my words: the other side of 14:23
decisions.reason: Jesus states the reverse of what he has just said. It also answers Judas: the world does not love him and does not keep his word, and so the Father and the Son do not come to make their home with it.

decisions.choice: my words ... the word: Jesus's teaching, first as many sayings, then as one message
decisions.reason: The plural "words" and the singular "word" refer to the same teaching (compare 14:23). John moves between the two without a change of sense, as in 12:47-48.

decisions.choice: not mine but the Father's: the message comes from the Father, who sent Jesus
alternatives: Jesus disowns the words as not his own
decisions.reason: Jesus does not deny that he speaks these words. He says where they come from: he speaks only what the Father who sent him has given him to say (7:16; 8:28; 12:49-50; 14:10). So to reject his word is to reject the Father's.

decisions.choice: it belongs to the Father (B); does not come from me. It comes from the Father (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "not mine but of the Father". Balanced says the word belongs to the Father; Readable says where the message comes from, which is what being the Father's word means here (meaning decision m3). Readable says "teaching" and "message" for "words" and "word", as in 14:23.

decisions.choice: es del Padre (B); Viene del Padre (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m3). "Mía" is a possessive and takes no setting.
